# Explained corpus changes

Every change of a corpus golden (`corpus/goldens/<id>.edges`) is explained here, one entry per changed reference, before the golden is rewritten. `npm run corpus` fails on any change no entry explains, and `npm run corpus:update` refuses to rewrite a golden while one is unexplained. The oracles (`npm run corpus:oracles`) read the same file: a disagreement with a language's own resolver is explained the same way when it is a known limit or a limit of the oracle.

An entry is a list item of exactly this form:

```
- `<repository>` `<kind>` `<from>:<line>` `<target>`: <reason>
```

- The repository, `<repository>`, is an id of `corpus/manifest.json`.
- The kind, `<kind>`, is `+` for a reference the golden lacks, `-` for a reference of the golden that is gone, or `<oracle>:<disagreement>` for an oracle (`typescript:false-edge`, `typescript:recall-loss`, `typescript:mismatch`, `python:false-edge`, `cargo:mismatch`, `cargo:crlf`, `go:false-edge`, `go:recall-loss`, `go:mismatch`, `csharp:recall-loss`, `csharp:false-reach`, `c:false-edge`, `c:unreadable`).
- The site, `<from>:<line>`, is the referencing file and line; `*` for the line explains every line of that file with that kind and target. Use it only where every such line has the same cause.
- The target, `<target>`, is the file the reference resolves to (for an oracle: the specifier, the field, or the project the disagreement is about).
- The reason says why: the change that made it, named by its commit or merge on the branch that carries it, or why the difference is right.

A list item that opens with a backtick and does not read this way, or names a repository the manifest does not hold, fails the run, so a mistyped entry cannot explain nothing in silence. A change that touches the edges of a language regenerates the goldens of the corpus repositories in that language in the same commit (`npm run corpus:update -- --only <id>`) and adds its entries under a heading of its own. Two changes that touch one golden are reconciled by regenerating it on the merged tip and keeping both sets of entries.

## From 1.0.0 to release 1.1.0

The goldens were made with the `v1.0.0` tag's `dist/` and then with each first-parent merge of `release/1.1.0` in turn, and each changed reference is attributed to the merge after which it last changed. A merge's subject names the work it carries. Removed references: 21 in google-cloud-python and 12 in poetry, all standard-library imports (`import logging`, `import json`) that bound to a same-named directory of the repository; 387 in react and 6 in jest, bare names that bound to a package.json no workspace declares (react's compiler playground imports `react` from its own dependencies, not from `packages/react`). No other reference of 1.0.0 is gone.

### Merge f2ad16b

Changed: C#: the directive line of a plain using alias inside a namespace body reads its target in the nearest namespace only, so an alias whose target lies farther out gives no edge on that line; every line that uses the alias keeps its edge (ruling csharp-unused-alias-silence-over-false-edge of the Althing 6.2.0 loop).

- `eShop` `-` `tests/Ordering.UnitTests/Application/OrdersWebApiTest.cs:5` `src/Ordering.API/Application/Queries/OrderViewModel.cs`: merge f2ad16b; the alias `Order` is used on lines 110, 119 and 120 of the same file, which keep their edges to the same target

## Oracle disagreements at release 1.1.0

What `npm run corpus:oracles` reports on the tip of `release/1.1.0` that is a known limit of Runes, a choice Runes makes on purpose, or a limit of the oracle itself. The Go and C# oracles need `go` and a .NET SDK and run in CI; their disagreements, if any, are added from the first CI run.

- `gin` `go:false-edge` `binding/binding_test.go:21` `github.com/gin-gonic/gin/testdata/protoexample`: go list ./... leaves out every directory named testdata, but the Go toolchain still imports a package there by its import path, and gin's own tests compile with this import, so the edge Runes gives is right and the oracle's package list is short
- `gin` `go:false-edge` `context_test.go:33` `github.com/gin-gonic/gin/testdata/protoexample`: go list ./... leaves out every directory named testdata, but the Go toolchain still imports a package there by its import path, and gin's own tests compile with this import, so the edge Runes gives is right and the oracle's package list is short

## Corpus gaps closed after release 1.1.0 began

### Gap 1: the first referenced tsconfig serves a file

Fixed: a file that several referenced tsconfig projects include takes the `paths` of the first one in the order of `references`, where Runes had stayed silent when the projects disagreed.

- `airflow` `+` `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/tests/e2e/fixtures/asset-data.ts:22` `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/tests/e2e/fixtures/index.ts`: the first referenced tsconfig that includes a file serves it, so the `tests/*` and `*` paths of the UI tsconfig.app.json bind the import (tsserver takes the first project in the order of `references`, and tests/** is included by tsconfig.app.json before tsconfig.dev.json)
